title: Actions to Reinforce Common ASEAN Position on South China Sea Issue
what_it_is: Actions to Reinforce Common ASEAN Position on South China Sea Issue

sections.label: ASEAN consensus on South China Sea
sections.summary: ASEAN's last consensus position on the South China Sea was reflected in the Chairman's Statement after the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in Vientiane in February this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: ASEAN's last consensus position on the South China Sea was reflected in the Chairman's Statement following the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in Vientiane in February this year.

sections.label: ASEAN unity and South China Sea
sections.summary: ASEAN Member States and China reaffirmed their relationship and underscored ASEAN unity, centrality, peace, stability and freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Member States and China broadly reaffirmed the importance of our multi-faceted and mutually beneficial relationships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also underscored the importance of ASEAN unity and centrality on issues of common interest to ASEAN, including the absolute need for peace and stability and freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea.

sections.label: Singapore coordinating ASEAN-China relations
sections.summary: As ASEAN-China coordinator, Singapore will support ASEAN-led processes to manage South China Sea tensions, preserving ASEAN unity while advancing ties with China, including the DOC and a Code of Conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As the current country coordinator for ASEAN-China relations, Singapore will fully support and we will facilitate the existing ASEAN-led processes to manage or to help manage the tensions in the South China Sea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will continue to perform this role in a transparent and objective manner, with the aim of preserving ASEAN unity and credibility whilst simultaneously advancing our multi-faceted and mutually beneficial relationship with China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This includes the full and effective implementation of the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (DOC) and the expeditious conclusion of a legally-binding Code of Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (COC).

sections.label: Non-claimant state and rules-based order
sections.summary: Singapore is not a claimant state and has no dispute with China, and stands for a rules-based world order based on international law, not might or size.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As I have said, first, we are not a claimant state, fortunately, so we have no dispute with China.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: What we stand for is we believe in a rules-based world order where decisions are made on the basis of law, on the basis of international law and not on the basis of might or size.

sections.label: Freedom of navigation and global trade
sections.summary: Freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea matter because at least five trillion dollars' worth of global trade flows through it, so stakeholders should not escalate tensions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Third, we need freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea because the South China Sea is a crucial avenue through which at least five trillion dollars' worth of global trade flows through it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is not enough to just talk about freedom of navigation and overflight but we all know that there needs to be a sense of security and stability, so that people who are transiting goods, services, flowing through the South China Sea will be able to do so with some certainty and clarity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This, therefore, makes it very important that all stakeholders do not unnecessarily escalate tensions in order to make a point because such escalation of tensions will have a profound impact on global trade and will affect even non-claimant states like us.
